qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: High advisor and client switching costs protect the wealth management franchise (retention >98%). AUM-based advisory wrap fees scale with asset appreciation and inflation. 5-year median ROIC is 13.8% and ROE has averaged 17-19% across market cycles. Primary erosion risk is regulatory scrutiny on cash-sweep deposit spreads and competition from independent RIA aggregators.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 6 (Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet). High-quality wealth management platform with sticky advisor relationships and AUM-based toll fees, but fails Gate 6 because Raymond James Bank and TriState Capital Bank maintain $58.9B in deposits and $51.3B in commercial and residential loans on $12.5B of equity (7.0x balance sheet leverage). Reliance on fractional-reserve bank leverage, deposit retention, and cash-sweep net interest income violates the Munger peace-of-mind fortress balance sheet standard. [5-10Y g: advisor recruiting/AUM growth 5.0% + fee mix 1.0% + net share repurchases 1.5%]
qualitative.evidence: Founded in 1962 and public since 1983, Raymond James Financial generated ~$12.8B in consolidated net revenues in FY2025, driven by the Private Client Group (~$10.2B) and Bank segment (~$1.78B net revenues, $1.715B NII). ROE has been consistently high (17.7% in FY2025, 18.9% in FY2024, 17.7% in FY2023, 17.0% in FY2022, 18.4% in FY2021) with a 5-year median ROIC of 13.8%. The wealth management franchise benefits from ~8,800 financial advisors and >$1.4T in client assets with high retention. However, total assets stand at $88.2B supported by $58.9B in bank deposits and $51.3B in loans against $12.5B in equity (~7.0x leverage). Fractional-reserve banking operations and cash-sweep net interest income tie earnings to interest-rate spreads and credit/deposit risks, failing Gate 6 under the Munger criteria.

evaluation_metadata.verdict: Rejected – G6 Cash & Fortress Balance Sheet
